transcript.text: Hello, I'm here to help you get ready for your appointment. Could you tell me what has been bothering you?
It's a dizziness, really — I feel light-headed and swimmy when I stand up, like I'm about to faint. It happens when I get up out of a chair or get out of bed.
When did this dizziness first start?
Oh, it's been going on for months, I think.
Have you ever had an allergy or a bad reaction to a medicine?
No, I don't think so. I've never had a bad reaction to any medicine that I know of.
How much does the dizziness affect your daily life?

It's a nuisance, I'd say about a 6 out of 10. I nearly fell once and had to grab the kitchen worktop, though I haven't actually gone down. I've stopped going to my Tuesday lunch club because I'm worried about feeling faint on the bus.
Have you started any new medicines or had any changes to your usual medicines recently?
Yes, I did start a new blood-pressure tablet — amlodipine, 5 mg once a day. The practice nurse added it about two and a half weeks ago because my readings were high.
Have you ever had any operations?
No, I've never had an operation. I do have arthritis in both hips, but that's just been managed with paracetamol.
Whereabouts do you feel the dizziness — and does it stay in that one spot or spread anywhere else?
It's not in one spot, really — it's more a general swimmy feeling in my head, like I'm about to faint, rather than the room spinning round.
Is there anything else you’ve noticed along with the dizziness that you haven’t mentioned yet?
No, nothing like that — no chest pain, no palpitations, no blackouts, and my arms and legs feel normal, no weakness.
What would you most like us to help you with today about the dizziness?
I'm worried the new tablet is what's causing it, and I'd like to know whether I should stop taking it.
Is there anything else about your health in the past that you'd like to add?
I've had high blood pressure for about 15 years, that's the main thing. And the arthritis in both hips, as I mentioned. Nothing else I can think of.
Are there any other medicines you're taking that we haven't talked about yet — including anything you buy without a prescription, like vitamins or supplements?

Yes, there are a few. I take a water tablet, bendroflumethiazide, 2.5 mg every morning — I've been on that for years. And I take a small tablet for my stomach each morning, but I can't remember its name. And paracetamol, 1 gram up to three times a day for my hip pain. I don't take any vitamins or supplements.
Can you tell me how the dizziness first came on — did it start all of a sudden, or did it come on slowly over time, or you're not sure?
Actually, now that I think about it properly — it started about 10 days ago. It came on roughly a week after I began that new blood-pressure tablet.
I want to make sure I've got this right — earlier you said the dizziness started a few months ago, and then you said it began about 10 days ago. Which one is closer to what actually happened?
The 10 days is right — I'm sorry, I do get muddled sometimes. It started about 10 days ago, roughly a week after I started the new tablet. The "months" was me misremembering.
Just to be sure — is there anything else you'd like to add about your medicines?
No, that's the lot. Just those four — the amlodipine, the water tablet, the stomach tablet, and the paracetamol.
Thank you, that is very helpful. I have put together a short summary of what you told me. Please read it and tell me if anything should be corrected before it goes to your doctor.
